verdictBasis: The new contracts close the byte-level PLAN-ID-V1 envelope, reproduce the exact PlanIntent and PlanId vectors independently, assign RequestId to one host owner, preserve the stored-view zero-attempt boundary, and keep both identity claims honestly IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED. They do not yet close the original implementer forks. PLAN-ID-V1 has no closed Rust semantic-universe schema or provider-bearing golden and depends on an unspecified SnapshotId recipe; its retained validator accepts noncanonical and arbitrary nested inputs. PLAN_ID_* and REQUEST_ID_ALLOCATION_FAILED outcomes have no exact route through D9's closed cause/code vocabulary. RequestId's broad semantic-exclusion claim is specified in prose but is mechanically joined only to PlanId. A separate stale product checker rejects the otherwise-consistent layer-4 decision and lets that dirty base contaminate its mutation suite.

findings.title: PLAN-ID-V1 has no closed Rust semantic-universe record and no provider-bearing oracle
findings.statement: preimageFields[9] says each TypeScript or Rust provider contributes a complete provider-specific universe. semanticUniverseSchemas contains only typescript-v1. The Rust project-model prose and DELIVERY handshake list concepts, but no binding record names exact Rust fields, nested shapes, digest representations, ordering, constants, or DELIVERY-to-Plan mapping. The sole positive PlanId vector has semanticUniverses=[], capabilityGrants=[], and no provider contribution even though the supported full profile contains both semantic providers. R6-PROBE-01 shows that an arbitrary Rust universe can replace that empty array and be blessed by recomputed oracles without a retained finding.
findings.impact: Two Rust hosts can encode different field names or omit different toolchain/cfg/package dimensions and still claim PLAN-ID-V1. The original cross-process identity fork survives on a required v1 provider path.
findings.requiredChange: Add a closed rust-v1 universe schema with exact field names/types/canonicalization and explicit mappings from the signed release, Rust provider handshake, resolved cfg/package/build-script state and grant. Add at least one shipping-full-profile PlanId oracle containing both TypeScript and Rust universes, plus omission/substitution/order negative controls and a checker mutation that arbitrary Rust fields cannot survive.

findings.title: PlanId is exact only conditional on an unspecified SnapshotId
findings.statement: PLAN-ID-V1 tag 1 requires a 'canonical SnapshotId string', C-2 says the host allocates SnapshotId at snapshot-binding, and DELIVERY transports a sealed Snapshot manifest. No live binding contract defines the SnapshotId text grammar, domain/version, manifest field closure, path/symlink/config-input canonicalization, digest recipe, or supplied-versus-recomputed verification. The PlanId golden supplies a synthetic snap1:sha256:000... value rather than deriving it from a snapshot oracle.
findings.impact: Independent hosts can construct different SnapshotIds for identical sealed bytes, producing different PlanIds while each follows the current documents. Cache, replay, evidence and provider VFS joins remain implementation-defined one level upstream of PLAN-ID-V1.
findings.requiredChange: Bind SNAPSHOT-ID-V1 with a closed manifest/preimage, path and symlink policy, domain/version/hash/text form, host verification rule, exact positive/transformation/negative vectors and the PLAN-ID-V1 join. The PlanId oracle should consume a derived SnapshotId from that vector rather than an unexplained placeholder.

findings.title: The retained PlanId encoder does not enforce most declared nested canonicalization
findings.statement: The binding prose requires sorted/unique scope sets, contribution activations, provider universes, grants and workflow set fields, with closed nested records. _plan_record_errors validates only the top-level field set, release shape, invocation profile, resolvedConfiguration ordering and commitment text before passing the remaining objects directly to CVE1. R6-PROBE-02 demonstrates that a noncanonical scope order can become a new accepted oracle. The checker likewise does not validate provider record shapes, contribution record closure, capability-grant closure, workflow field types/order or budget key/unit closure.
findings.impact: The checker can certify two semantic encodings that the prose says must collapse to one canonical descriptor. A persisted PlanDescriptor reader or second implementation has no executable rejection oracle for these cases.
findings.requiredChange: Implement complete recursive PlanDescriptorV1 validation/canonical construction against live C-2, DELIVERY and configuration schemas. Add exact negative controls for unsorted/duplicate scope arrays, contributions, universes, grants and workflow sets; unknown nested fields; invalid budget units; and provider substitutions. Refuse a self-test unless the base is clean.

findings.title: Identity validation and allocation outcomes have no exact D9 cause/code mapping
findings.statement: PLAN-ID-V1 creates PLAN_ID_INVALID_REPRESENTATION, PLAN_ID_PREIMAGE_SCHEMA_VIOLATION, PLAN_ID_MISMATCH, PLAN_ID_PROFILE_VIOLATION and PLAN_INTENT_COMMITMENT_MISMATCH, then says only to route them through the live D9 validation/fault mapping. REQUEST-ID-V1 creates REQUEST_ID_ALLOCATION_FAILED after collision exhaustion and calls it operational without naming a D9 faultCause/errorCode. D9 requires every operational-failed or request-rejected termination to derive its code from one closed cause map; no identity-allocation or host-invariant cause exists, and context can distinguish a corrupt stored plan from a fresh host-planning defect. R6-PROBE-03 and R6-PROBE-04 show that mutually different mappings are checker-indistinguishable.
findings.impact: The first CLI implementation must invent public termination semantics or misuse ledger-corrupt, config-invalid or host-io. This violates D9's total-mapper rule and the freeze litmus that forbids implementer-created exit mappings.
findings.requiredChange: For each identity outcome and provenance context, bind the exact D9 domainCondition, cause family/value, class and public code. If D9 lacks an honest host-invariant or identity-allocation fault, version D9's closed vocabulary and add goldens, total-map checks and DELIVERY-style cross-contract mutations. Specify CSPRNG/reservation failures as well as collision exhaustion.

findings.title: The exact RequestId exclusion list is not joined to eight of its nine claimed semantic surfaces
findings.statement: REQUEST-ID-V1 normatively excludes RequestId from SnapshotId, PlanId, fact/finding identity, FactViewId, EvidenceDigest/proofs, RunId, sealed Run semantics, Coverage/verdict/termination and cache/regeneration keys. check-operability.py verifies the list text and only one live join: RequestId is absent from PLAN-ID-V1's excluded identities. Its sole semantic-participation fixture inserts RequestId into PlanId. The checker does not load the fact-identity, evidence or R-1 contracts and there is no same-semantic-input/different-RequestId vector over the named identities and outcome. R-1 currently proves that property for ExecutionId, not RequestId.
findings.impact: The prose is implementable and correctly keeps assurance at IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED, but the adjudication's broad negative-control claim is not load-bearing. A later edit can leak RequestContext into facts, evidence, Run identity or policy while every retained RequestId check stays green.
findings.requiredChange: Add cross-contract design-integrity joins and a RequestId-variation fixture spanning every identity/result recipe that exists. Bind RequestContext as host metadata outside SealedStageInput, close unknown fields on evidence/identity manifests, and explicitly park surfaces whose recipes do not yet exist rather than claiming they are mechanically protected.

findings.title: The layer-4 decision converged in the contracts but its product checker still targets the superseded provisional shape
findings.statement: product-dispositions.v1.json and resolved-inputs.v2.json both bind CI_IGNORES_LAYER_4: CI does not load/resolve layer 4 and does not reject mere presence; local-interactive keys resolved values and provenance. check-product-dispositions.py still requires configuration.untrackedOverridePosture.provisionalShipDefault.rule, which no longer exists after bindingProductDecision replaced the provisional branch. Normal validation therefore emits PD-RI. The mutation self-test does not first refuse a dirty base, so unrelated mutations are reported rejected by the pre-existing PD-RI failure.
findings.impact: The semantic product decision is not reopened, but the retained design-integrity signal is false and architecture-freeze verification cannot be green honestly.
findings.requiredChange: Join the checker to bindingProductDecision and PRODUCT_DECIDED, delete the obsolete provisional requirement, and add the same clean-base refusal used by the other retained mutation suites before evaluating isolated mutations.

confirmedRepairs.evidence: The independent encoder matched the domain, u16 recipe/count, all thirteen tag/u32 frames, CVE1 values, SHA-256 text form, one positive and two transformation vectors. CVE1 map ordering, array ordering and NFC rejection behaved as specified.

All three commitments matched independently. The analysis path stores one commitment across AttemptRecord, ExecutionPlan and PlanId input; the stored-view path commits for validation/correlation but creates no attempt, ExecutionPlan, PlanId or new Run. The remaining Snapshot/Rust/D9 findings are separate.

The TypeScript record names the signed manifest/profile, exact runtime/provider artifacts and descriptor digests, protocol/build/runtime/compiler/platform identity and resolved inputs, and DELIVERY binds the matching one-shot worker. No provider-bearing PlanId vector executes that schema yet.

PRODUCT and RESOLVED-INPUTS agree that CI ignores and never loads layer 4 while local-interactive keys it. The independent layer-4 PlanId transformation matched. R6-L4-01 is an integration-instrument defect, not a reopened product choice.

confirmedRepairs.evidence: Host ingress ownership, pre-parse reservation, req1_ lowercase 128-bit form, fresh-candidate collision retry, external/internal retry split, stored-view lifecycle, RequestContext propagation, operational/audit custody and semantic-exclusion intent are explicit. Assurance is honestly IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED. R6-XID-04 and R6-IP02-01 prevent seal.

Both contracts remain IMPLEMENTABLE / IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED with empty qualificationEvidenceIds and releaseEvidenceIds. check-assurance.py passes and rejects all 12 assurance mutations. No green checker is treated as product qualification or demonstration.

findingStatus.evidenceGrade: IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED for the primitive envelope only
findingStatus.reason: The exact framing/hash oracle is real, but the required Rust provider input and upstream SnapshotId are not closed, nested canonical validation is not executable, and identity failures have no D9 mapping. An implementer still has to invent persisted cross-process identity behavior.

Allocation, representation, collision retry, custody and stored-view behavior are specified. The collision/allocation failure cannot be projected through D9 without invention, and the exact semantic-exclusion set is not mechanically joined beyond PlanId.

minimumBeforeRereview: Bind SNAPSHOT-ID-V1 and a closed rust-v1 semantic-universe schema, then add a full-profile provider-bearing PlanId golden.
Make recursive PlanDescriptorV1 canonicalization and validation executable, with negative controls for every set/order/nested-schema rule.
Bind every PLAN_ID_* and RequestId allocation failure to an exact D9 cause/class/code, versioning D9 if its closed vocabulary lacks an honest cause.
Add RequestId variation/cross-contract exclusion fixtures for the semantic identities and outcomes the contract names, parking any recipe that does not yet exist.
Repair check-product-dispositions.py to consume bindingProductDecision and refuse mutation self-testing on a dirty base.
Run the repaired normal and mutation suites, then obtain an independent rereview without reusing the retained Python encoders.
